chapter_title: Concerning the Seed Grain that shall be formed by
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:** This interior truth and this natural good of truth shall be formed and [GAP-1] and perfected by the five essential faculties of the spiritual life. Now, love and the absence of love sustain the interior truth and the whole perception from which it grows. So, just as these spiritual nourishments sustain it [GAP-2] it perishes [GAP-3] through [GAP-4] the deprivation that comes from the absence of all good.

**¶3:** In this way also the Divine Good operating through truth gathers the five essential faculties of the spirit unto itself and unites them.

**¶4:** In this way too, a spiritual deficiency and a privation of good shall arise from state to state through these faculties when they are separated; and those who have received the Divine Good by free choice have gathered it inward and perfected it and made it their own, while spiritual temptation and suffering shall arise for it through those who have refused.

**¶5:** Minds also shall be led into falsity on account of these things, through the active power of the corporeal and self-loving nature that dwells within them. It has cast its obscurity over them — that is, the darkness of self-love has veiled their understanding — just as it shall also cast its obscurity over the essential goods and truths themselves and corrupt the works that proceed from all perceptions of truth.

---

*Translator's note:* The "five elements" in this oldest cosmological layer correspond to the five constituent faculties or powers of the regenerating mind — roughly: understanding, thought, reflection, will, and reasoning — which together compose the spiritual life. Their gathering by "righteousness" (¶3) describes the unification of these faculties under the Divine Good, while their dispersal (¶4–5) describes the fragmentation that occurs when the corporeal nature — here called "Matter" — imposes its shadow, which is the obscurity of self-love and falsity from evil, over the whole perceptive life.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: This seed grain and this barley grain shall be formed and [nourished] and beautified by the five elements. Now, the warmth and the cold nourish the seed grain and the entire tree. So, just as these things nourish it [so also] it is destroyed [and consumed] through [great] hunger.
In this way also righteousness gathers the five to it.

In this way too, a lack and a shortfall shall occur from place to place through them; and they who have chosen it have gathered it in and beautified and attained it, while an affliction shall arise for it through those.

People also shall be caused to stumble on their account, through the energy of Matter that dwells in them. It has poured its shadow over them, just as it shall also pour its shadow over the elements and destroy the fruits of all the trees.

fills.explanation: The triad "formed, nourished, and beautified" mirrors the Swedenborgian regeneration sequence (implantation, sustenance, perfection) and fits the agricultural register — seeds are formed, nourished by the elements, and brought to beauty/fruition; the very next sentence confirms this by discussing how warmth and cold "nourish" the seed.

The sentence structure "just as these things nourish it... it is destroyed" requires a contrastive-correlative connector; "so also" is the standard Kephalaia formula completing a "just as... so also" comparison, here turning from nourishment to destruction.

The Kephalaia consistently uses paired verbs of destruction; "destroyed and consumed" is a standard doublet in this register, corresponding spiritually to the complete perishing that follows total privation of good, and staying within the agricultural imagery of hunger devouring what was once nourished.

The spiritual reading's "the deprivation that comes from the absence of all good" corresponds to an intensified hunger in the natural register; "great hunger" captures the totality of privation — complete spiritual famine — and is the standard Kephalaia intensifier for afflictions of lack.
